Across Niagara

Open across all 12 Niagara municipalities.

NiASPIRE is for high school students in Grades 9–12 right across Niagara Region. Wherever you live in Niagara, your school, your business and your community can take part.

St. Catharines Niagara Falls Welland Fort Erie Grimsby Lincoln Niagara-on-the-Lake Pelham Port Colborne Thorold Wainfleet West Lincoln

How the rollout works: The 2027 pilot starts in St. Catharines, Welland and Niagara Falls, where the first schools, mentors and retail partners are coming together. Students from all 12 municipalities can take part in the pilot, and schools and partners in every municipality are welcome to join from the start — so Fort Erie, Grimsby, Lincoln, Niagara-on-the-Lake, Pelham, Port Colborne, Thorold, Wainfleet and West Lincoln are part of NiASPIRE from day one, with in-person programming expanding across the region as more local partners join.

The name

What NiASPIRE stands for

Every letter of NiASPIRE carries a part of the mission. Ni is Niagara — the region this program serves — and the six letters of ASPIRE are the six pillars students, schools and partners will see in everything NiASPIRE does.

Ni —

Niagara

Niagara Region, Ontario — home to the students, schools and communities NiASPIRE serves, across all 12 municipalities.

A —

Achievement

Encouraging academic excellence and measurable improvement.

S —

Skills

Preparing students for careers, entrepreneurship, technology and leadership.

P —

Prevention

Reducing risk factors associated with crime, substance misuse and school disengagement.

I —

Rewarding effort through shopping credits, prepaid cards and other opportunities.

R —

Resilience

Strengthening mental well-being, confidence and positive life choices.

E —

Empowerment

Developing responsible young leaders through civic education, mentorship and community participation.

The full meaning

NiASPIRE: Niagara Achievement, Skills, Prevention, Incentives, Resilience & Empowerment.

NiASPIRE is the short name for the Niagara Youth Achievement & Opportunity Initiative. Our slogan: Learn. Earn. Lead.

The model

Six pillars hold the whole program up.

Tap a pillar to see what it means in practice. Together they cover the full journey: achieve and improve, build skills, stay on a positive path, earn real incentives, grow resilience, and step up empowered as a young leader.

Incentives · How it works

Four steps, plain numbers, no fine-print surprises.

1

Get nominated

A teacher, school or community partner puts a Grade 9–12 student forward for excellence, improvement or commitment.

2

Show the progress

Grades, effort, attendance and commitment are reviewed each cycle — improvement counts, not just top marks.

3

Earn the reward

Students earn restricted shopping credits to spend at participating local retailers — see the table below.

4

Build what's next

Skills training, a mentor and job shadowing turn one reward into momentum for school, work and leadership.

What a student can earn

AchievementWhat it meansPer cycle
ExcellenceOutstanding achievement in a cycle$100
ImprovementClear, verified progress from the student's own starting point$100
Growth routeSustained effort and commitment on the way up$75
Yearly capMaximum per student, across both cycles in a year$200 / year

Rewards are shopping credits for participating local retailers — not cash. Schools confirm each award with NiASPIRE before credits are issued.

Incentives · Rewards, step by step

How rewards are delivered

Earning a reward is only part of it. Here is how credits move from achievement in the classroom to something a student can actually use — safely, through their school, and only at approved local retailers.

1

Earn — achievement that counts

Students earn shopping credits for achievement, improvement and commitment, verified through their school each reward cycle. Excellence and verified improvement earn $100 in a cycle, the growth route earns $75 — up to the $200 yearly cap.

2

Receive — gift cards & vouchers in the pilot

During the 2027 pilot, rewards are delivered as retailer gift cards or controlled vouchers, issued after the school confirms the award. The NiASPIRE Opportunity Card is a planned later phase — a single student card for holding and spending credits once it is ready.

3

Spend — local, approved, purposeful

Credits are restricted to approved local retailers and school-related needs — not cash. That keeps rewards spent locally and on things that support school, learning and well-being, up to the $200 per-student yearly cap.

Concept design — the Opportunity Card is a future phase of NiASPIRE.

Shown as a concept only. It is not available now, and no card, account or payment service is being offered. In the 2027 pilot, rewards arrive as retailer gift cards or controlled vouchers.

Skills · Skills Academy

Future skills students can actually use.

40 academy seats are part of our 2027 pilot goals. Training is practical and portfolio-based — students leave with work they can show, not just a certificate.

Grades 9–12

Artificial Intelligence

Using AI tools responsibly for school, projects and work — what they do, where they fail, and how to check them.

Grades 9–12

Digital Marketing

How local businesses reach customers online: social, search, email and simple campaigns students help run for real.

Grades 9–12

Photography & Video

Shooting, lighting and editing on phones and cameras — building a small portfolio across the academy term.

Grades 9–12

Content Creation

Planning, scripting and publishing content with a positive voice — plus the business basics behind creator work.

Plus, for every pilot student: a mentor, and access to career exposures and job-shadowing placements with Niagara employers — 20 are part of our 2027 pilot goals.

Why it matters

Recognition early. Better paths for longer.

NiASPIRE is prevention through achievement: catch young people doing the right thing, reward it visibly, and surround them with skills, adults and opportunities that make the positive path the rewarding one.

🛡️ Prevention — steer toward the positive path

Prevention means reducing the risk factors associated with crime, substance misuse and school disengagement. Give Niagara youth recognition, structure, mentors and real opportunity early, so they are steered toward positive leadership — and away from:

  • Drugs and substance misuse
  • Gang involvement and exploitation
  • Homelessness and housing instability
  • Drifting away from school and community

🌱 Resilience — confidence and well-being

Resilience means strengthening mental well-being, confidence and positive life choices — so setbacks become reasons to keep going, not reasons to give up.

  • Earlier support and a sense of belonging, before difficulties become mental-health crises
  • Confidence built on real, verified achievement
  • Positive life choices backed by mentors and community

⭐ Empowerment — step up, serve, be heard

Empowerment develops responsible young leaders through civic education, mentorship and community participation. Students who earn rewards are invited to lead: peer encouragement, school and community projects, and civic life.

  • Student leadership and peer mentoring roles
  • Community service and showcase events
  • Nonpartisan civic engagement — how councils, boards and public decisions work, and how young people can take part, without party politics

For partners

Concrete ways to get involved — pick one.

Every partner gets a specific role and a clear time commitment. Choose the way that fits you best, and we'll talk it through in a briefing first.

🏢 Host a career showcase

Open your workplace for one session so students can see real jobs in Niagara up close.

👀 Host a job shadow

Take one student for a half-day or full-day shadow from the 20 planned pilot placements.

🎤 Lead a workshop

Teach one Skills Academy session — AI, marketing, media, trades, business or your own field.

⭐ Become a mentor

Meet a student regularly through the school year, with program structure and school oversight.

🎁 Sponsor a reward cycle

Fund student rewards for a cycle — $100 covers one student's reward for one cycle; $200 covers a full year. We'll explain how sponsorship works in your briefing.

🛍️ Become a retail partner

Accept NiASPIRE shopping credits at your store and be part of where rewards are redeemed locally.

Not a partner? Find your place

Straight answers

Questions partners ask first.

How can I support NiASPIRE?
NiASPIRE is incorporating as a non-profit organization. Sponsorship and partnership enquiries are welcome — book a partner briefing to discuss how to support the 2027 pilot.
What are the numbers on this page?
120 students, 40 Skills Academy seats, 20 career exposures and 2 reward cycles are our 2027 pilot goals — the scale we're building toward across all 12 Niagara municipalities.
Which communities can take part?
All 12 Niagara municipalities: St. Catharines, Niagara Falls, Welland, Fort Erie, Grimsby, Lincoln, Niagara-on-the-Lake, Pelham, Port Colborne, Thorold, Wainfleet and West Lincoln. The 2027 pilot starts in St. Catharines, Welland and Niagara Falls, with students from all 12 municipalities able to take part and schools and partners in every municipality welcome to join.
Who can earn a reward — only top students?
No. NiASPIRE deliberately rewards three things: excellence, improvement from a student's own starting point, and commitment through the growth route. A student moving from struggling to steady can earn the same $100 cycle reward as a top achiever.
What can shopping credits be spent on?
Credits are spent at participating local retailers, not handed out as cash. Participating stores are listed with each reward cycle.
What is the Opportunity Card?
The Opportunity Card is a student card for holding and spending reward credits, currently in development. We'll share full details here as soon as they are confirmed with our partners.
Is NiASPIRE political?
No. The Empowerment pillar includes nonpartisan civic engagement — helping young people understand how local decisions are made and how to take part — with no party affiliation or campaigning.
